mechanism: Methylene blue is a potent oxidant that causes severe hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients. Also, paradoxically, it is used to treat methemoglobinemia but is CONTRAINDICATED in G6PD deficiency because it requires NADPH for its action (G6PD-dependent) — it will be ineffective and cause hemolysis.
alternatives: For methemoglobinemia in G6PD patients: ascorbic acid (vitamin C), exchange transfusion

mechanism: Fava beans contain vicine and convicine, which are hydrolyzed to divicine and isouramil — potent oxidants that cause favism (acute hemolytic anemia) in G6PD-deficient individuals. This is one of the most common preventable triggers in southern China. Hemolysis typically occurs 12-48 hours after ingestion. Even inhalation of fava bean pollen can trigger hemolysis in highly sensitive individuals.
alternatives: All other legumes are generally safe including soybeans, mung beans, chickpeas, lentils, peas
Green beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) are botanically distinct and safe
